title: 'Patients are ready for this': New study reveals 90% of NHS staff use AI at work — and most patients are…
excerpt: AI is conquering the health sector
content_html:
• Report claims 90% of NHS staff are using AI to assist with their work
  • Heidi survey points to high AI use across healthcare
  • AI looks to reduce the burden on healthcare professionals

NHS staff are increasingly using AI tools to improve workflows and handle admin tasks, and claim that patients are positive about the development, new research has claimed.

A survey of 1,000 healthcare professionals working in the NHS by Heidi found 90% of respondents revealing they are using AI in clinical work, with healthcare professionals driving the change, with nearly two-thirds (65%) adopting AI to assist in their workflow.

Rising administrative burdens in recent years may have contributed to the use of AI to assist in tasks, although it seems some AI use is happening regardless of official policies.

AI helps with the admin

Of those surveyed, 94% have increased their AI use at work in the past year, or kept it the same. Among hospital doctors, pharmacists, and mental health professionals, however, the figure is 96%.

The results of the survey clearly demonstrate a wide take-up of AI tools, no doubt driven by an increase of administrative tasks (experienced by 80% of respondents) which includes increased demand for documentation, particularly among nurses (61%), pharmacists (63%) any by GPs dealing with referrals and letters (52%).

While it is being used for drafting referrals and notes, AI is also being used to manage patient follow-ups (66%), and there is a belief that the technology is prolonging careers, by making the workload more manageable.

Dr Hannah Allen, Chief Medical Officer and GP at Heidi, said: "These findings reflect what we hear every day from patients and clinicians. Patients are ready for this, and healthcare professionals have already made AI part of how they manage a workload that has grown well beyond what most would call sustainable.”

Policies and oversight

Use of computers and patient data within the NHS has been closely monitored for years, and in recent years the challenges of AI have been highlighted, with various trusts implementing policies to handle generative AI use. Among these are the NHS AI Lab Code of Conduct, NHS England's Blueprint for AI in Health and Social Care, and the Information Governance (IG) Frameworks for handling patient data and other sensitive information.

So, the 35% expressing concern over patient privacy should be able to consult their local policies and procedures to ensure that their work doesn't infringe what has been put in place by the organization.

The march of AI across healthcare seems to be almost complete, and regardless of which tools are used, those governance policies should ensure admin is managed, data is kept private, and patient care continues to be the central focus.

content_html_zh:
• 报告称 90% 的 NHS 工作人员正在使用人工智能来协助他们的工作
  • 海蒂调查表明人工智能在医疗保健领域的使用率很高
  • 人工智能希望减轻医疗保健专业人员的负担

新研究称，NHS 工作人员越来越多地使用人工智能工具来改进工作流程和处理管理任务，并声称患者对这一发展持积极态度。

Heidi 对 1,000 名在 NHS 工作的医疗保健专业人员进行的调查发现，90% 的受访者表示他们正在临床工作中使用人工智能，医疗保健专业人员推动了这一变革，近三分之二 (65%) 采用人工智能来协助他们的工作流程。

近年来不断增加的行政负担可能促使人们使用人工智能来协助完成任务，尽管无论官方政策如何，似乎都有一些人工智能的使用。

AI 帮助管理

在接受调查的人中，94% 的人在过去一年中增加了人工智能在工作中的使用，或者保持不变。 然而，在医院医生、药剂师和心理健康专业人员中，这一比例为 96%。

调查结果清楚地表明，人工智能工具得到了广泛采用，这无疑是由于管理任务的增加（80%的受访者经历过）所致，其中包括对文件的需求增加，特别是护士（61%）、药剂师（63%）以及处理转诊和信件的全科医生（52%）。

虽然人工智能被用于起草转诊和笔记，但它也被用于管理患者随访（66%），并且人们相信该技术可以通过使工作量更易于管理来延长职业生涯。

海蒂首席医疗官兼全科医生汉娜·艾伦博士说：“这些发现反映了我们每天从患者和临床医生那里听到的情况。 患者已经为此做好了准备，医疗保健专业人员已经将人工智能纳入他们管理工作量的一部分，而工作量的增长远远超出了大多数人所说的可持续水平。”

政策和监督

NHS 内计算机和患者数据的使用多年来一直受到密切监控，近年来，人工智能的挑战日益凸显，各种信托机构纷纷实施政策来处理生成式人工智能的使用。 其中包括 NHS 人工智能实验室行为准则、英国 NHS 健康和社会护理人工智能蓝图，以及用于处理患者数据和其他敏感信息的信息治理 (IG) 框架。

因此，对患者隐私表示担忧的 35% 的人应该能够查阅当地的政策和程序，以确保他们的工作不会违反组织制定的规定。

人工智能在医疗保健领域的进步似乎已基本完成，无论使用哪种工具，这些治理政策都应确保管理得到管理、数据保密以及患者护理仍然是中心焦点。
